rationale: The buyer is clear and well-resourced — IT admins at mid-market enterprises with hybrid AD environments face real, recurring helpdesk cost when SSPR fails, and the adjacent market (Cayosoft, Semperis) proves willingness to pay at $thousands/year. However, operational_autonomy scores only 5: accurate SSPR diagnostics require reading live Azure/AD telemetry, interpreting configuration state, and often guiding per-tenant remediation — this is closer to a managed-service or consulting engagement than a hands-off SaaS, which caps autonomy well below the 7-floor needed for build. The build_gate on operational_autonomy and buildability_with_ai are both unmet; promote to validate to confirm whether a lighter monitoring-only product (not full remediation) could achieve automation.
solution_plan: The service is an automated SSPR/Writeback health monitor: it ingests Azure Entra audit log exports (CSV or via Graph API connector) and runs a Claude-powered diagnostic that flags misconfiguration patterns, missing writeback agent heartbeats, and audit gaps — delivering a weekly email report to the IT admin. Build: the factory builds a Claude prompt pipeline that parses uploaded audit logs, a minimal landing page with a Stripe payment link ($49/mo), and an intake form asking for tenant domain + log file upload; no operator coding. Sell: reach IT admins via targeted posts on r/sysadmin, r/azure, and ServerFault answers, plus cold outreach to IT managers at companies advertising hybrid AD roles on LinkedIn; outreach batch goes out only after Youval approves. Maintain: log uploads trigger automated Claude analysis and email delivery; billing runs via Stripe; the only recurring human step is approving the weekly outreach batch. Caution: the real diagnostic value requires live API access to Azure/Entra, not just log uploads — if customers demand agent-level integration rather than log-based analysis, operational_autonomy drops further and this becomes a build Youval cannot maintain solo without significant engineering.
notes: build_gate failures: operational_autonomy=5 (floor 7) and buildability_with_ai=5 (floor 6). A log-upload-only MVP may meet buildability but autonomy remains constrained by the per-tenant diagnostic complexity.
